summary_html: Agency makes an **indicated** finding of abuse/neglect — in Illinois an "indicated report" is one where "an investigation determines that credible evidence of the alleged abuse or neglect exists" (325 ILCS 5/3); Illinois does not use the words *substantiated* or *founded* (325 ILCS 5/7.12). This decision often unlocks **court petitions**, **service mandates**, and **federal reporting** duties.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Lyon v. Department of Children & Family Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that DCFS violated Lyon's due process rights by combining the low credible-evidence standard for indicating a report and deciding the first-stage appeal with delays beyond its own regulatory deadlines, and affirmed expungement from the State Central Register.
key_cases.relevance: The controlling Illinois authority on the process due before a substantiated (indicated) finding may stand on the central register.
key_cases.quote: we require strict statutory and regulatory compliance only if the Department uses the credible-evidence standard to indicate a report and to consider a first-stage appeal

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court largely upheld injunctive relief requiring DCFS to weigh exculpatory evidence under the credible-evidence standard and to give child-care workers a pre-deprivation conference and expedited appeal, while holding foster parents lack a protected liberty or property interest.
key_cases.relevance: The controlling federal decision on the process due before DCFS enters and discloses an indicated finding.
key_cases.quote: It also requires that the investigator take into account all of the available evidence that tends to show that abuse or neglect did or did not occur.

key_cases.case_name: Doyle v. Camelot Care Centers, Inc.
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that the credible-evidence standard combined with a belated post-deprivation hearing denied child-care workers adequate process when DCFS disclosed indicated findings to their employers, though the individual DCFS defendants were immune and the private employers were not state actors.
key_cases.relevance: Identifies the occupational liberty interest at stake when DCFS indicates and discloses a finding against a child-care worker.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that the credible evidence standard, operating in conjunction with a belated post-deprivation hearing, failed to afford adequate process to Ms. Doyle and Mr. Konold

key_cases.case_name: Burris v. Department of Children & Family Services
key_cases.holding: The court reversed, holding that once a court has entered a judicial finding of child neglect on the same issue, section 7.16 of the Reporting Act and DCFS Rule 336.190(a)(3) require dismissal of an administrative appeal seeking expungement of the indicated report.
key_cases.relevance: A juvenile-court neglect finding forecloses the parallel administrative route for contesting the indicated register entry.
key_cases.quote: plaintiff's administrative appeal requesting expungement of the report of child neglect should have been dismissed pursuant to section 7.16 of the Reporting Act

key_cases.holding: The court held that the circuit court could not disregard a DCFS administrative abuse finding by conducting its own de novo review, reversed the change of custody as against the manifest weight of the evidence, and reinstated DCFS as guardian with power to consent to adoption.
key_cases.relevance: An indicated administrative finding retains probative force in later juvenile-court proceedings and cannot simply be ignored.
key_cases.quote: The court, without authority, rejected an administrative finding that the Wards abused Austin after conducting a de novo review of the matter.

common_failures: Insufficient credible evidence for an indicated finding (325 ILCS 5/3)

timeline_requirements.deadline: 60 days to determine "indicated" or "unfounded"; extendable in additional periods of up to 30 days for good cause (325 ILCS 5/7.12)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Report may be deemed "undetermined" where a complete investigation was not possible (325 ILCS 5/7.12)

timeline_requirements.requirement_name: Request to amend or expunge an indicated report
timeline_requirements.deadline: 60 days, tolled until any related criminal or juvenile court action concludes (325 ILCS 5/7.16)
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Date of the Department's notice that the investigation is complete
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Loss of the departmental hearing to amend or remove the report from the State Central Register (325 ILCS 5/7.16)
